newsitem.title: USA: Triton sets $310 mln 97 capital budget.
newsitem.headline: Triton sets $310 mln 97 capital budget.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said on Tuesday it approved a 1997 capital program of $310 million, up 29 percent from the $240 million spent in 1996.
The company said most of the spending has been allocated to development of significant oil and gas reserves in the Gulf of Thailand and Colombia.

"During 1997, Triton will embark upon a period of unprecedented growth resulting from substantial progress on the development of our assets in the Gulf of Thailand and Colombia," said Thomas Finck, Triton's chairman and chief executive.

He said investment in the development of the oil and gas resource base, estimated at 836 million barrels of oil equivalent, positions Triton for "substantial improvement" in future production, earnings and cash flow.

The company said $150 million of Triton's capital spending program is allocated for the development of the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields in Colombia, compared with $146 million in spent in 1996. Triton said it expects oil production from the two fields to reach at least 500,000 barrels per day by the end of 1997, nearly tripling the current rate.

About $95 million has been earmarked for initial development of the Cakerawala Field, the first of four natural-gas discoveries Carigali-Triton Operating Co (CTOC) has made on Block A-18 in the Malaysia-Thailand joint development area in the Gulf of Thailand.
In 1996, Triton spent $52 million was spent in the Gulf of Thailand.

Most of the remaining $65 million is allocated to worldwide exploration activities including drilling wells in China, Colombia, Ecuador, Guatemala and other locations, the company said, up from the $42 million spent in 1996.
